content:
[Goal]

- Since the clash is about the comparison between an "original" recipe and a "test / given" recipe, I wonder if the first sentence of the Goal section can be made clearer - that the player's task is to compare between the original recipe and the recipe prepared by the robot, instead of "whether the robot followed the recipe correctly".

- Please add: "blocks separated by a line : {{NEXT}}. Each block has one or more steps." You may delete the corresponding constraint afterward.

- (Rules) For clarity, please what "respecting" the order of the blocks means. Or, perhaps you could change "respected" -> "preserved".

- (Rules) Please specify that the check for identical steps is case-sensitive.

- (Rules) It is currently unclear from the rules whether respecting the block order means that steps cannot simply "jump" between blocks. For example, is this considered a perfect recipe or a mess?

Add flour                             Add egg
Add egg                               Whisk until smooth
NEXT                                    NEXT
Whisk until smooth           Add flour

How about this?

Add flour             Add flour
Add milk              Add milk
Add egg               NEXT
NEXT                    Add egg
Stir in batter       NEXT
                              Stir in batter

The wording for the last two rules might need to be revisited.

[Constraints]

- Currently, all tests/validators have O, T < 10. Any plans to include cases where O, T is a larger number (up to 20 as per your constraints)? Similarly, any plans to include longer step descriptions (up to 100)? Please revise your constraints accordingly otherwise.

- Please change all instances of "instruction" to "step" to be consistent with the rest of the clash.

- Please state that each step only contains alphanumeric characters and spaces.

- I think the constraint "A recipe never begins or ends with {{NEXT}}" (as suggested by @5DN1L) seems somewhat redundant, since there exists another constraint "Every block contains at least one instruction" that makes the {{NEXT}} line appearing at the beginning/end of a recipe impossible.

[Cases]

- Please include a pair of test/validator cases that check for case sensitivity in step validation (i.e. Add milk != ADD MILK).

- In the test case "Not Really", the original recipe contains a NEXT line while the test recipe does not. I expected the output to be "Invalid Recipe" as the number of steps are not equal, but your output is "It's a mess!". Does this mean that the NEXT line is an actual step? How does this work?

- Can steps contain the word NEXT? If a line with only a single word "NEXT" is used to separate recipe blocks, does "   NEXT    " count as a step?

[Stub generator]

- As per your current constraints, please change 1024 to 100.

- Please include a write line in the stub generator: e,g, "write good recipe?".

Thank you :)

Binary output issue
* According to the contribution guidelines, binary outputs should be avoided for clashes. That's exactly the issue with your clash, as it allows only two possible answers (either "Perfect Recipe" or "It's a mess!"). Please modify the output requirement to allow for more than two possible answers.

Goal / Output
* Please format "NEXT", "Perfect Recipe" and "It's a mess!" as {{constants}} instead of in <<bold>>.

Output
* Please remove the quotation marks.

Constraints
* Please specify the upper bounds of O and T.

Cases
* These cases are the same:
  • No Next (Validator 8)
  • Not Really (Test 11)

* All cases should be different. At the same time, each test and its validator should cover the same scenario (e.g. Test 1 covers an all-good scenario, so Validator 1 should also cover that scenario) but with slightly different inputs.

Thanks.
Please also switch the status of the clash back to WIP. Thanks.

Good points. There's a few things you mentioned that I think are clear enough (but they could be clearer). Also, I don't know if this puzzle has been edited at all since your comment.

Jumping between blocks would not really be respecting the order of the blocks; however, it wouldn't hurt to clear up any confusion by changing the last rule to:
'- Every step from each reference recipe block must appear exactly once in the corresponding tested recipe block.'

Case "Not Really" - you can sort of deduce that 'NEXT' counts a step because it is included in the O and T variables, but that can be made more obvious by changing the first two lines in [Input] to "...number of steps in the (original/test) recipe".

I don't think there's any reason for a step to contain 'NEXT'  but, if they choose to, it should be pretty clear that blocks are only separated by a line that reads 'NEXT'. I wouldn't recommend including things like '  NEXT  ' because it wouldn't be a valid part of any recipe so would have to be a block separator, and anyone for whom that would be a challenge will already be struggling with the parsing and condition handling.


Unrelated, I'd love to see shortest mode turned on.

Thanks for you answer, however i was wondering, are the validator test executed randomly then ? 
I didn't want people to hardcode the answer's order
I don't think the validators are executed in a random order. However, players aren't shown the validators during a clash either.

I'm wondering if you could keep your contribution in WIP a bit longer and wait until the reviews are finished before switching its status?

Constraints
* Please add these constraints:
  • A recipe never begins or ends with {{NEXT}}.

  • Every block contains at least one instruction.

  • 0 < length of an instruction < 100

* Please move the first constraint to the end, so that the order of the constraints matches the order of the inputs.

* Please change "recipe instruction" to "instruction in the original recipe", since instructions in the test recipe are not necessarily unique.

Cases
* Pair 1 ("All good") and Pair 5 ("Lot of mixing" and "Valid with multiple ingredients") cover the same scenario, but Pair 5 has a better design, so please:

  • Move Pair 5 to the front and make it the new Pair 1.

  • Revise the original Pair 1 so that it instead covers the scenario where the original and test recipes are identical multi-block recipes (i.e. the instructions appear in exactly the same order).

* Wrong Order (Test 2): Please move "Add 10g salt" to the beginning of the test recipe, o that it covers the same scenario as Validator 2 instead of duplicating the scenario already covered by Pair 6.

* Please split Pair 10 ("Easy Recipe" and "One Block") into two pairs of single-block recipes:

  • One pair (2 cases) where the instructions appear in the same order.
  
  • One pair (2 cases) where the instructions appear in a different order.

* Pair 12 ("Not sure about this one" and "Contains"): This largely duplicates Pair 8, so please remove it.

* Please add a new pair of cases for each of the scenarios below (try to make the first block always the same):

  • Similar to Pair 7 ("Very Jammy" and "Extra Time Same Step"), but with the duplicate instructions appearing in different blocks.

  • The original and test recipes are identical multi-block recipes, except that the test recipe contains one extra NEXT.

  • The original and test recipes are identical multi-block recipes, except that the test recipe has one NEXT removed.

  Adding these new case pairs will also help reduce the proportion of "It's a mess!" cases to below half of the total.

Thanks.
